tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative-ish framing ('Use this skill when an endpoint is Failed...') and lists many explicit trigger contexts across real-time, serverless, async and batch transform scenarios, covering symptoms users would describe without naming SageMaker internals directly. It is a dense paragraph but stays within a reasonable length for the breadth of scope it covers, and it focuses on user-facing symptoms (slow, erroring, not scaling, costs too much) rather than internal implementation of the skill itself.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when an endpoint is Failed or never passes its health check, cannot read its model artifact from S3 or KMS, is unreachable from a private subnet, returns ModelError or 5xx, does not scale out, or sits idle while billed; when a serverless endpoint cold-starts or throttles; when async requests never notify, back up or fail on large inputs; when a transform job fails to parse records, times out or reports Completed with records missing

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body jumps directly into SageMaker-specific checks, APIs, metric namespaces, and quirks that an agent would not already know, without explaining general ML or AWS concepts.
tests.evidence: 'Load [api-quirks.md] before interpreting any response that looks clean, empty, InService or Completed' — this is domain-specific knowledge, not general explanation.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference data (check catalog table, router table) is summarized as index/pointer tables with check-ids and severities, but the full detection rules, remediations, and citations are explicitly deferred to references/checks-sagemaker-inference.md. The tables in the body are concise what-it-catches summaries, not full reference material.
tests.evidence: 'Load checks-sagemaker-inference.md before writing any finding: it holds the full detection rules, remediations, and citations.'

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All six reference files are linked via markdown links in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is paired with explicit conditions for when to load it, e.g. tied to steps, symptoms, or response types.
tests.evidence: 'Load [api-quirks.md] before interpreting any response that looks clean, empty, InService or Completed' and 'Load [known-causes.md] whenever the user names an error or symptom'.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (guardrails, read-only enforcement, severity rules) are highly prescriptive, while judgment-heavy areas (right-sizing, fit decisions) explain reasoning and allow workload-specific judgment.
tests.evidence: 'Never invent a threshold... marked workload-specific and reported as INFO' alongside strict guardrails like 'Never call UpdateEndpoint... or any other mutating API.'

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill doesn't present multiple competing tools for the same task without guidance; routing tables map specific symptoms to specific APIs/checks rather than offering equal alternatives.
tests.evidence: Router table maps one specific API per symptom, e.g. 'DescribeEndpointConfig DataCaptureConfig, ListMonitoringSchedules' — no competing equal options presented.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The Review Procedure and Router teach generalizable approaches (identify area, read config, check scaling, etc.) that apply across any endpoint/job, not one-off instance-specific declarations.
tests.evidence: 'Step 1: Identify the area and enumerate resources.' through 'Step 8: Assemble findings and the report.' — a generalizable procedure applicable to any SageMaker inference review.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has a dedicated 'Common wrong answers' section plus an 'Error Handling' section documenting non-obvious API quirks and misleading responses, functioning as gotchas.
tests.evidence: '"The endpoint is InService, so it's serving traffic and the queue is fine." InService is control-plane state; a real-time, async or serverless variant can be InService with CurrentInstanceCount = 0...'

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill provides output templates in assets/ for each area (real-time, serverless/async, batch) referenced for full reports.
tests.evidence: '[endpoint-health-report-template.md](assets/endpoint-health-report-template.md) — load when a full real-time endpoint report is requested.'

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large inline output templates appear in the body; actual templates are stored in assets/ and referenced conditionally.
tests.evidence: Body only references templates, e.g. 'use the template for the area' — no inline template skeleton is embedded.

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All three asset files are referenced in the body.

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each asset link specifies the exact condition under which it should be loaded (full report request for a specific area).
tests.evidence: '[endpoint-health-report-template.md](assets/endpoint-health-report-template.md) — load when a full real-time endpoint report is requested.'

tests.name: Asset path format

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The procedural Review Procedure is presented as a checkbox checklist with Step N format, and the detailed sections below reference the same step numbers (Step 1, Step 2, etc.).
tests.evidence: '- [ ] Step 1: Identify the area and enumerate resources.' ... '### Step 1 — Identify the area' ... '### Step 2 — Read the configuration'

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit self-validation gate before presenting output, checking findings against the catalog, evidence, namespaces, and disclosure requirements.
tests.evidence: '## Before You Present — Validate Your Own Output ... Before presenting, re-check your output against this list. Treat it as a gate, not a suggestion.'
